title: Thailand Restores Visa-Free Entry for India in Revised 30-Day Framework
excerpt: After a brief scare that left Indian travellers uncertain, Thailand's cabinet has added India to its revised 30-day visa exemption list alongside Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Malta and the Maldives.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Thailand reinstated visa-free entry for India, effective 15 days after Royal Gazette publication.
  • Total countries eligible for visa-free tourism now stands at 65, up from 60.
  • Indian tourists stay an average of 7.2 days, fitting well within the new 30-day limit.
  • The decision follows a decline in Indian tourist arrivals after initial visa changes.
  • Thailand aims to balance security concerns with tourism growth through revised visa policies.

  • Thailand's cabinet on July 14 approved adding India, Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Malta and the Maldives to a revised 30-day visa-free entry scheme, reversing an earlier plan that would have stripped India of visa-free access.
  • The move brings the total number of countries and territories eligible for visa-free tourism entry to 65 under a restructured framework that replaces the previous 60-day scheme for 93 nations.
  • Indian tourists — Thailand's third-largest source market — stay an average of just 7.2 days, making the 30-day window more than sufficient for most visitors.
  • The new rules will take effect 15 days after publication in Thailand's Royal Gazette; until then, the existing 60-day visa-free arrangement remains in force.

India Added Back After Tourism Dip

Thailand's cabinet on July 14, 2026, approved the inclusion of India in a revised 30-day visa-free tourism entry scheme, according to Deputy Government Spokesperson Ploytalay Laksameesangchan. The decision reverses weeks of uncertainty that had rattled Indian travellers and the tourism industry after Bangkok announced a sweeping overhaul of its visa-free programme in May.

India joins Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Malta and the Maldives in the updated 30-day visa exemption category. The six additions bring the total number of countries and territories covered under the scheme to 59 for the 30-day tier, with Mauritius and Seychelles receiving 15-day visa-free access and Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia eligible for visa on arrival — 65 nations in all.

"The cabinet has approved a 30-day visa-free stay to better match the travel patterns of Indian visitors, who remain an important market for Thailand."

— Surasak Phancharoenworakul, Thailand's Tourism and Sports Minister

From 60 Days to Confusion to Clarity

The backstory is one of policy whiplash. Thailand introduced its 60-day visa-free entry scheme for 93 countries in July 2024, a move that sharply boosted arrivals. But on May 19, 2026, the cabinet approved a plan to scrap the 60-day arrangement entirely, citing security concerns. Officials said extended visa-free periods had been exploited by some foreign nationals for unauthorised employment, nominee business operations and involvement in transnational scam networks, including call-centre fraud.

"The government noted that Indian visitors stay an average of just 7.2 days per trip, well within the 30-day limit."

"The government noted that Indian visitors stay an average of just 7.2 days per trip, well within the 30-day limit."

"The government noted that Indian visitors stay an average of just 7.2 days per trip, well within the 30-day limit."

Under the initial May proposal, the number of countries eligible for visa-free access would have dropped from 93 to 54 for the 30-day tier, with the visa-on-arrival programme slashed from 31 nations to just four. India was initially slated to be moved to the visa-on-arrival category, capping stays at 15 days — a significant downgrade from the 60-day allowance it had enjoyed.

The announcement triggered confusion among Indian tourists and travel agents, according to reports from the Travel Trade Journal and other outlets. Arrivals from India — Thailand's third-largest source market after China and Malaysia — reportedly declined in the weeks following the May decision, prompting a rethink.

Why India Made the Cut

Thai authorities cited several reasons for restoring India's visa-free status. The government noted that Indian visitors stay an average of just 7.2 days per trip, well within the 30-day limit. India's importance to Thailand's economy, trade and investment relationships also weighed heavily, as did the decline in Indian visitor numbers after the initial announcement.

The extension of 30-day visa-free entry to all 27 European Union member states — achieved by adding Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus and Malta — was tied to Thailand's own diplomatic goal of securing Schengen visa exemptions for Thai passport holders, according to ASEAN NOW.

Impact of Visa Changes on Tourism
›Visa-free access restored for India after initial confusion.
›Tourist arrivals from India declined post-May visa announcement.
›Thailand's tourism sector generated nearly $80 billion in 2025.
›New rules aim to enhance security while promoting tourism.

Tourism remains a critical pillar of Thailand's economy. The sector generated nearly 0 billion from 33 million international visitors in 2025, while more than 16 million foreign tourists had visited the country by July 4 of this year, according to CurrentIndia. From January to May 10, 2026, Thailand received 12.4 million foreign tourists — a 3.43% decrease compared to the same period last year, Reuters reported.

What Indian Travellers Need to Know

The revised framework has not yet taken effect. The draft Ministry of Interior announcements will be published in the Royal Gazette, and the new rules will come into force 15 days after publication. Until then, Indian passport holders can still enter Thailand under the existing 60-day visa-free arrangement.

Once implemented, Indian citizens visiting for tourism purposes will be allowed to stay for up to 30 days without a visa. All visitors to Thailand must complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) at least three days before arrival — a requirement that has been in place since May 1, 2025. The government has also announced plans to tighten TDAC screening by linking agency databases to better assess traveller risk.

Passports must have at least six months of validity remaining. Travellers planning stays longer than 30 days will need to apply for an appropriate visa through Thailand's e-visa system.

A Broader Crackdown With a Tourism Buffer

The restructuring is part of Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's broader effort to close security loopholes without killing the tourism goose. The government has adopted a "one country, one entitlement" approach to eliminate overlapping visa categories.

"This review is not intended to reduce tourism opportunities, but to adjust the system to make it more appropriate, clear and verifiable."

— Ploytalay Laksameesangchan, Deputy Government Spokesperson

For the Indian diaspora, the outcome is a net positive. The 60-day window was generous but rarely utilised; most Indian visitors use Thailand for short holidays, weddings and business trips that comfortably fit within a 30-day stay. And unlike the brief period of uncertainty in May and June, when India's visa-free status appeared to be on the chopping block, the country now has a clear, confirmed pathway to hassle-free entry. The key is to keep an eye on the Royal Gazette for the official effective date.
